{{Short description|German physicist (born 1952)}}
{{Primary sources|date=July 2023}}
'''Hermann Nicolai''' (born 11 July 1952 in [[Friedberg, Hesse|Friedberg]]) is a German theoretical physicist and director emeritus at the [[Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics]] in [[Golm (Potsdam)|Potsdam-Golm]].

==Education and career==
At [[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology]], Hermann Nicolai, beginning in 1971, studied [[physics]] and [[mathematics]] with a ''[[Diplom]]'' in 1975 with a doctorate in 1978 under the supervision of [[Julius Wess]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Hermann Nicolai |url=https://academictree.org/physics/peopleinfo.php?pid=715947 |website=Physics Tree}}</ref> At [[Heidelberg University]], Nicolai was an assistant in [[theoretical physics]] from 1978 to 1979. From 1979 to 1986, he worked at [[CERN]] in [[Geneva]] as a staff member in the theory department. In 1983 he received his [[habilitation]] at [[Heidelberg University]]. He was a [[Academic ranks in Germany|professor (with civil service grade C3)]] of theoretical physics at Karlsruhe Institute of Technology from 1986 to 1988 and from 1988 to 1997 a [[Academic ranks in Germany|professor (with civil service grade C4)]] of theoretical physics at the [[University of Hamburg]]. At the [[Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics]], Nicolai was head of the department "Quantum Gravity and Unified Field Theories" and a director from 1997 to 2020, when he retired as director emeritus.<ref name="homepage2">{{cite web |title=Professor Dr. Dr. h. c. Hermann Nicolai, Curriculum Vitae |url=https://www.aei.mpg.de/300646/homepage-of-hermann-nicolai |website=Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics (Albert Einstein Institute)}}</ref> Between 2017 and 2024, he led the research group "Exceptional Quantum Gravity" at the Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics, which was funded by an Advanced Grant of the [[European Research Council]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Exceptional Quantum Gravity |url=https://www.aei.mpg.de/306486/exceptional-quantum-gravity |access-date=2026-09-24 |website=www.aei.mpg.de |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Exceptional Quantum Gravity {{!}} eQG {{!}} Project {{!}} Fact Sheet {{!}} H2020 |url=https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/740209 |access-date=2026-09-24 |website=CORDIS {{!}} European Commission |language=en}}</ref>

He was a member of the editorial board of ''[[Communications in Mathematical Physics]]'' from 1993 to 1995. Then, from 1998 to 2003 the editor-in-chief of the journal ''[[Classical and Quantum Gravity]]'', and from 2006 to 2011 the editor-in-chief of the journal ''[[General Relativity and Gravitation]]'', jointly with George Ellis.<ref>{{Cite web |title=General Relativity and Gravitation – Editorial Board – Editors-in-Chief |url=https://link.springer.com/journal/10714/editorial-board |access-date=2026-10-08 |website=link.springer.com}}</ref>

In 1991, Nicolai received the [[Klung Wilhelmy Science Award|Otto-Klung-Award (now called the Klung Wilhelmy Science Award)]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=2014-10-02 |title=Award Winners in Physics |url=https://www.klung-wilhelmy-wissenschafts-preis.de/en/preistraeger/preistraeger_physik/index.html |access-date=2026-09-25 |website=www.klung-wilhelmy-wissenschafts-preis.de |language=en}}</ref> in 2010 the [[Albert Einstein Medal]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Einstein Society 2503 – Einstein Haus Bern |url=https://www.einstein-bern.ch/einstein-society/ |access-date=2026-09-25 |language=en-GB}}</ref> and was awarded the 2012 [[Gay-Lussac-Humboldt Prize]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Homepage: Hohe Ehrung für Hermann Nicolai |url=https://www.tagesspiegel.de/potsdam/landeshauptstadt/hohe-ehrung-fur-hermann-nicolai-7353583.html |access-date=2026-09-25 |work=Der Tagesspiegel Online |language=de-DE |issn=1865-2263}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Gay-Lussac Humboldt Prize |url=https://www.abg.asso.fr/en/article/515/515-prix-scientifique-franco-allemand-gay-lussac-humboldt |access-date=2026-09-25 |website=www.abg.asso.fr |date=4 June 2026 }}</ref> He was appointed an honorary professor at the [[Humboldt University of Berlin]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. Dr. rer. nat. Herrmann Nicolai - Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin |url=https://www.hu-berlin.de/en/people-detail-page/prof-dr-rer-nat-herrmann-nicolai |access-date=2026-09-25 |website=www.hu-berlin.de}}</ref> and in 2005 at the [[Leibniz University Hannover]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Honorarprofessuren in den Fakultäten |url=https://www.uni-hannover.de/universitaet/profil/ehrungen/von-der-leibniz-universitaet-verliehene-auszeichnungen/honorarprofessuren |access-date=2026-09-25 |website=Leibniz Universität Hannover |language=de}}</ref> In 2016 he was awarded an honorary doctorate from [[Chalmers University of Technology]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-09-04 |title=Honorary Doctors through the years |url=https://www.chalmers.se/en/about-chalmers/traditions-and-celebrations/honorary-doctors/ |access-date=2026-09-25 |website=www.chalmers.se |language=en}}</ref>

Nicolai's research in the context of [[Theory of everything|unified theories]], cosmology, and the Big Bang has been covered repeatedly in various media and was featured on a 1999 cover of [[Der Spiegel]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=DER SPIEGEL 30/1999 - Inhaltsverzeichnis |url=https://www.spiegel.de/spiegel/print/index-1999-30.html |access-date=2026-09-25 |website=www.spiegel.de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Interview mit dem Physiker Hermann Nicolai: "Ein großes Rätsel bleibt" |url=https://www.tagesspiegel.de/potsdam/landeshauptstadt/ein-grosses-ratsel-bleibt-7360363.html |access-date=2026-09-25 |work=Der Tagesspiegel Online |language=de-DE |issn=1865-2263}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2017-07-17 |title=Die Formel für jedes Problem: die Weltformel |url=https://radiocorax.de/die-formel-fuer-jedes-problem-die-weltformel/ |access-date=2026-09-25 |work=Radio Corax}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Wissenschaftsgeschichte: Heisenbergs Weltformel |url=https://www.spektrum.de/news/heisenbergs-weltformel/1542469 |access-date=2026-09-25 |website=www.spektrum.de |language=de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=ZEIT |first=DIE |date=2005-04-14 |title=Alles nur Fassade |url=https://www.zeit.de/2005/16/Nicolai-Interview |access-date=2026-09-25 |work=Die Zeit |language=de-DE |issn=0044-2070}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Astrophysiker Nicolai über den Anfang des Universums: "Wir sind so unvorstellbar unbedeutend" |url=https://www.tagesspiegel.de/gesellschaft/wir-sind-so-unvorstellbar-unbedeutend-8416882.html |access-date=2026-09-25 |work=Der Tagesspiegel Online |language=de-DE |issn=1865-2263}}</ref>

== Research ==
Nicolai's research is in the fields of [[supersymmetry]], [[supergravity]], and [[Particle physics|particle]] and [[astroparticle]] physics, [[M-theory]], [[Cosmic singularity|cosmic singularities]], and [[general relativity]].

=== Supersymmetry ===
In 1976 and 1977 Hermann Nicolai was the first to introduce supersymmetric quantum mechanics.<ref>{{Citation |last=Junker |first=Georg |title=Supersymmetric Quantum Mechanics |date=1996 |work=Supersymmetric Methods in Quantum and Statistical Physics |pages=7–19 |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-3-642-61194-0_2 |access-date=2026-09-24 |place=Berlin, Heidelberg |publisher=Springer Berlin Heidelberg |doi=10.1007/978-3-642-61194-0_2 |isbn=978-3-540-61591-0|url-access=subscription }}</ref> In this work Nicolai formulated a supersymmetric lattice model with only [[Majorana fermion|Majorana fermions]], similar to a supersymmetric version of the [[Sachdev–Ye–Kitaev model]].

Nicolai showed in 1980 that supersymmetric theories  can be formulated without [[Anticommutative property|anti-commuting variables]], in terms of a purely bosonic functional measure. This is achieved by integrating out fermions (using [[Berezin integral|Berezinian integration]]) and a non-linear and non-local field transformation of the bosonic fields.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Nicolai |first=Hermann |date=January 1980 |title=On a new characterization of scalar supersymmetric theories |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0370269380901380 |journal=Physics Letters B |language=en |volume=89 |issue=3–4 |pages=341–346 |doi=10.1016/0370-2693(80)90138-0 |bibcode=1980PhLB...89..341N |hdl=11858/00-001M-0000-0013-5E95-1 |hdl-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Nicolai |first=H. |date=December 1980 |title=Supersymmetry and functional integration measures |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0550321380904605 |journal=Nuclear Physics B |language=en |volume=176 |issue=2 |pages=419–428 |doi=10.1016/0550-3213(80)90460-5 |bibcode=1980NuPhB.176..419N |hdl=11858/00-001M-0000-0013-5E89-E |hdl-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Citation |last=Lechtenfeld |first=Olaf |title=The Nicolai-map approach to supersymmetry |date=2023 |arxiv=2309.00481}}</ref> This transformation became known as Nicolai map, which has recently become an area of active research with applications from quantum mechanics to multi-dimensional [[supersymmetric Yang–Mills theory]], and most recently, supergravity.

=== Supergravity ===
In 1982 Nicolai and [[Bernard de Wit]] derived the SO(8) gauged "[[N = 8 supergravity|''N'' = 8 supergravity theory]]",<ref>{{Cite web |last=cern |date=2017-01-13 |title=The many lives of supergravity |url=https://cerncourier.com/a/the-many-lives-of-supergravity/ |access-date=2026-10-22 |website=CERN Courier |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |title=Half a century of supergravity: bridging between Einstein and the quantum |date=2026 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-1-009-57589-8 |editor-last=Ceresole |editor-first=A. |location=Cambridge, United Kingdom |editor-last2=Dall'Agata |editor-first2=Gianguido}}</ref> which is the maximally supersymmetryic theory in four space-time dimensions with one [[graviton]] and no particles with a [[Spin (physics)|spin]] greater than 2. This is the most symmetric field theoretic extension of Einstein’s theory of general relativity and a candidate for the unification of gravity and matter into a unified theory of quantum gravity.

In the late 1980s H. Nicolai derived the first example of an [[Integrable system|integrable]] locally supersymmetric theory, by explicitly constructing a linear system for the bosonic and fermionic equations of motion of maximal supergravity in two space-time dimensions.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Nicolai |first=H. |date=August 1987 |title=The integrability of N=16 supergravity |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0370269387910720 |journal=Physics Letters B |language=en |volume=194 |issue=3 |pages=402–407 |doi=10.1016/0370-2693(87)91072-0 |bibcode=1987PhLB..194..402N |hdl=11858/00-001M-0000-0013-5D8F-4 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> With de Wit he also helped understand how [[Gauge theory|gauged]] N = 8 supergravity is embedded in N = 1 supergravity in eleven dimensions, by consistently [[Compactification (mathematics)|compactifying]] eleven-dimensional supergravity on the [[N-sphere|seven-dimensional sphere S<sup>7</sup>]] and correctly reproducing all non-linearities of the low-energy theory. New, general formulas for uplifting four-dimensional solutions to higher dimensions were derived.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=De Wit |first1=B. |last2=Nicolai |first2=H. |date=January 1987 |title=The consistency of the S7 truncation in d=11 supergravity |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0550321387902537 |journal=Nuclear Physics B |language=en |volume=281 |issue=1–2 |pages=211–240 |doi=10.1016/0550-3213(87)90253-7 |hdl=11858/00-001M-0000-0013-5DA7-E |hdl-access=free }}</ref>

In the 2000s, H. Samtleben and H. Nicolai introduced the embedding tensor formalism which allows a unified description of gauged supergravities of any type and in any space-time dimension, and which pointed to the existence of a new type of supergravity beyond d = 11.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Nicolai |first1=H. |last2=Samtleben |first2=H. |date=2001-02-26 |title=Maximal Gauged Supergravity in Three Dimensions |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.86.1686 |journal=Physical Review Letters |language=en |volume=86 |issue=9 |pages=1686–1689 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.86.1686 |pmid=11290224 |arxiv=hep-th/0010076 |bibcode=2001PhRvL..86.1686N |issn=0031-9007}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Nicolai |first1=Hermann |last2=Samtleben |first2=Henning |date=2001-04-17 |title=Compact and Noncompact Gauged Maximal Supergravities in Three Dimensions |url=http://stacks.iop.org/1126-6708/2001/i=04/a=022?key=crossref.83992c8c6925131210f4366004e41653 |journal=Journal of High Energy Physics |volume=2001 |issue=4 |pages=022 |doi=10.1088/1126-6708/2001/04/022 |arxiv=hep-th/0103032 |bibcode=2001JHEP...04..022N |issn=1029-8479}}</ref> they also constructed a large class of gauged supergravity theories in three dimensions and their symmetries.<ref>{{cite book |last1=De Wit |first1=Bernard |title=Proceedings of 27th Johns Hopkins Workshop on Current Problems in Particle Theory: Symmetries and Mysteries of M Theory — PoS(jhw2003) |last2=Nicolai |first2=H. |last3=Samtleben |first3=H. |year=2004 |page=016 |chapter=Gauged Supergravities in Three Dimensions: A Panoramic Overview |doi=10.22323/1.011.0016 |doi-access=free |s2cid=15349626}} [http://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0403014 arXiv.org]</ref>

=== Particle physics ===
Starting in the late 2000s, Hermann Nicolai and [[Krzysztof Antoni Meissner|Krzysztof A. Meissner]] explored how [[conformal symmetry]] can ensure that the [[Standard Model]] can remain viable up to the [[Planck scale]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Meissner |first1=Krzysztof A. |last2=Nicolai |first2=Hermann |date=May 2007 |title=Conformal symmetry and the Standard Model |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0370269307003486 |journal=Physics Letters B |language=en |volume=648 |issue=4 |pages=312–317 |doi=10.1016/j.physletb.2007.03.023 |arxiv=hep-th/0612165 |bibcode=2007PhLB..648..312M }}</ref> This proposal is consistent with the [[Supersymmetry#Current status|fact that no hints of low energy]] (N=1) supersymmetry have been found, despite decades of dedicated collider searches.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-09-06 |title=Supersymmetry's absence at LHC puzzles physicists |url=https://www.sciencenews.org/article/supersymmetrys-absence-lhc-puzzles-physicists |access-date=2026-10-08 |language=en-US}}</ref>

Later, Meissner and Nicolai explored a proposal made by [[Murray Gell-Mann]] in 1983 to explain the existence of three, and only three, generations of quarks and leptons from maximal supergravity.<ref>{{Cite book |title=Shelter Island II: proceedings of the 1983 Shelter Island Conference on Quantum Field Theory and the Fundamental Problems of Physics |date=1985 |publisher=MIT Press |isbn=978-0-262-10031-1 |editor-last=Jackiw |editor-first=Roman W. |location=Cambridge, Mass}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Meissner |first1=Krzysztof A. |last2=Nicolai |first2=Hermann |date=2018-08-31 |title=Standard Model Fermions and Infinite-Dimensional R Symmetries |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.121.091601 |journal=Physical Review Letters |language=en |volume=121 |issue=9 |article-number=091601 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.121.091601 |pmid=30230857 |arxiv=1804.09606 |bibcode=2018PhRvL.121i1601M |issn=0031-9007}}</ref> Their work can in principle explain the existence of the fermions observed in the Standard Model without [[Superpartner|superpartners]], and why there can be only three generations of them.

Nicolai's and Meissner's work led them to predict the existence of supermassive [[Gravitino|gravitinos]], hypothetical partners to the [[graviton]] with spin 3/2. Supermassive gravitinos are [[Dark matter]] candidates.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Meissner |first1=Krzysztof A. |last2=Nicolai |first2=Hermann |date=2019-08-02 |title=Planck mass charged gravitino dark matter |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevD.100.035001 |journal=Physical Review D |language=en |volume=100 |issue=3 |article-number=035001 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.100.035001 |arxiv=1809.01441 |bibcode=2019PhRvD.100c5001M |issn=2470-0010}}</ref> They could also explain the origin of [[Primordial black hole|primordial black holes]] via the condensation and gravitational collapse of "lumps" of supermassive gravitinos in the early [[radiation-dominated era]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Meissner |first1=Krzysztof A. |last2=Nicolai |first2=Hermann |date=2020-11-09 |title=Supermassive gravitinos and giant primordial black holes |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevD.102.103008 |journal=Physical Review D |language=en |volume=102 |issue=10 |article-number=103008 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.102.103008 |arxiv=2007.11889 |bibcode=2020PhRvD.102j3008M |issn=2470-0010}}</ref> With other colleagues, they proposed to search for supermassive gravitinos with the [[Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory|JUNO]] and [[Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment|DUNE]] underground detectors. They calculated the expected signatures of gravitinos in those detectors and showed that they significantly differ from the expected neutrino signals.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Kruk |first1=Adrianna |last2=Lesiuk |first2=Michał |last3=Meissner |first3=Krzysztof A. |last4=Nicolai |first4=Hermann |date=2025-08-13 |title=Signatures of supermassive charged gravitinos in liquid scintillator detectors |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/fm6h-7r78 |journal=Physical Review Research |language=en |volume=7 |issue=3 |article-number=033145 |doi=10.1103/fm6h-7r78 |arxiv=2407.04883 |bibcode=2025PhRvR...7c3145K |issn=2643-1564}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=A new candidate for dark matter |url=https://www.aei.mpg.de/1275865/a-new-candidate-for-dark-matter |access-date=2026-09-25 |website=www.aei.mpg.de |language=en}}</ref>

=== M-theory and E10 ===
[[M-theory]] is an attempt to mathematically unify all [[Consistency|consistent]] versions of [[superstring theory]]. In 1988 de Wit, Hoppe, and Nicolai showed that maximally supersymmetric [[Special unitary group|SU(∞)]] [[Matrix theory (string theory)|matrix theory]] can serve as a first concrete mathematical model of M-theory, following the earlier discovery that the eleven-dimensional supermembrane is the maximally extended theory of a supersymmetric relativistic extended object.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=de Wit |first1=B. |last2=Hoppe |first2=J. |last3=Nicolai |first3=H. |date=December 1988 |title=On the quantum mechanics of supermembranes |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0550321388901162 |journal=Nuclear Physics B |language=en |volume=305 |issue=4 |pages=545–581 |doi=10.1016/0550-3213(88)90116-2 |bibcode=1988NuPhB.305..545D |hdl=11858/00-001M-0000-0013-5D4D-7 |hdl-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bergshoeff |first1=E. |last2=Sezgin |first2=E. |last3=Townsend |first3=P.K. |date=April 1987 |title=Supermembranes and eleven-dimensional supergravity |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/037026938791272X |journal=Physics Letters B |language=en |volume=189 |issue=1–2 |pages=75–78 |doi=10.1016/0370-2693(87)91272-X |bibcode=1987PhLB..189...75B }}</ref> They constructed the theory as the N→∞ limit of a maximally supersymmetric quantum mechanical SU(N) matrix model. Subsequently it was shown that the associated Hamiltonian has a continuous spectrum, unlike the purely bosonic model.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=De Wit |first1=B. |last2=Lüscher |first2=M. |last3=Nicolai |first3=H. |date=June 1989 |title=The supermembrane is unstable |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0550321389902149 |journal=Nuclear Physics B |language=en |volume=320 |issue=1 |pages=135–159 |doi=10.1016/0550-3213(89)90214-9 |bibcode=1989NuPhB.320..135D |hdl=11858/00-001M-0000-0013-5D23-3 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>

In the early 2000s Nicolai did research on the roles of [[exceptional Lie groups]] and their role in M-theory. Together with Günyadin and Koepsell, Nicolai worked on conformal and quasiconformal realizations of exceptional Lie groups. They obtained the first explicit geometric realization of the maximal rank finite-dimensional exceptional Lie group <math>E_{8}</math>, and discussed possible applications to supergravity and M-theory.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Günaydin |first1=M. |last2=Koepsell |first2=K. |last3=Nicolai |first3=H. |date=July 2001 |title=Conformal and Quasiconformal Realizations¶of Exceptional Lie Groups |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/PL00005574 |journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics |language=en |volume=221 |issue=1 |pages=57–76 |doi=10.1007/PL00005574 |arxiv=hep-th/0008063 |bibcode=2001CMaPh.221...57G |issn=0010-3616}}</ref> By studying the [[BKL singularity|BKL limit]], [[Thibault Damour|Damour]], [[Marc Henneaux|Henneaux]], Kleinschmidt and Nicolai highlighted the central role of the maximal rank hyperbolic [[Kac–Moody algebra|Kac-Moody]] symmetry <math>E_ {10}</math> as a candidate symmetry for the unification of the fundamental interactions, in a concrete framework of [[Emergence|emergent]] spacetime.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Damour |first1=T. |last2=Henneaux |first2=M. |last3=Nicolai |first3=H. |date=2002-11-11 |title=E 10 and a Small Tension Expansion of M Theory |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.89.221601 |journal=Physical Review Letters |language=en |volume=89 |issue=22 |article-number=221601 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.89.221601 |pmid=12485059 |arxiv=hep-th/0207267 |issn=0031-9007}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Damour |first1=Thibault |last2=Kleinschmidt |first2=Axel |last3=Nicolai |first3=Hermann |date=2006-08-21 |title=K ( E 10 ), supergravity and fermions |url=http://stacks.iop.org/1126-6708/2006/i=08/a=046?key=crossref.f09ce72be9ab82eef63b8f75f66fad94 |journal=Journal of High Energy Physics |volume=2006 |issue=8 |pages=046 |doi=10.1088/1126-6708/2006/08/046 |issn=1029-8479|arxiv=hep-th/0606105 }}</ref> This model is supposed to replace spacetime dynamics and its concomitant symmetries in the Planck regime close to the [[Gravitational singularity|singularity]], where classical notions of spacetime are expected to break down. This would imply a purely algebraic description of the universe in cosmological spacetime regions near the singularity (within the [[Planck time]]) using the <math>E_{10}</math>-symmetry with spacetime symmetries and space-time based quantum field theory as emergent phenomena. This work also hints at the emergence of a mathematically well-defined non-[[computability]] near the cosmological singularity, which would make it impossible to reach the beginning of time in a finite number of mathematical steps.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Nicolai |first=Hermann |date=2021-09-16 |title=Complexity and the Big Bang |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1361-6382/ac1b07 |journal=Classical and Quantum Gravity |volume=38 |issue=18 |pages=187001 |doi=10.1088/1361-6382/ac1b07 |arxiv=2104.09626 |bibcode=2021CQGra..38r7001N |issn=0264-9381}}</ref>

In 2022, Kleinschmidt and Nicolai showed that in maximal d = 11 supergravity the [[Wheeler–DeWitt equation|Wheeler-DeWitt]] [[Hamiltonian mechanics|Hamiltonian]] for the bosonic part coincides with the unique quadratic [[Casimir operator]] of <math>E_ {10}</math> at low levels.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Kleinschmidt |first1=Axel |last2=Nicolai |first2=Hermann |date=2022-04-15 |title=The E10 Wheeler-DeWitt operator at low levels |url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/JHEP04(2022)092 |journal=Journal of High Energy Physics |language=en |volume=2022 |issue=4 |article-number=92 |doi=10.1007/JHEP04(2022)092 |issn=1029-8479|arxiv=2202.12676 }}</ref> This eliminates quantization ambiguities in conventional approaches to define the Wheeler-DeWitt equation and in principle allows constructing (infinitely many) [[Observable|observables]]. They also studied various finite-dimensional truncations to show that the Wheeler-DeWitt functional generically vanishes on classical singularities.<ref name=":1">{{cite journal |last1=Kleinschmidt |first1=Axel |last2=Koehn |first2=Michael |last3=Nicolai |first3=Hermann |year=2009 |title=Supersymmetric quantum cosmological billiards |journal=Physical Review D |volume=80 |issue=6 |article-number=061701 |arxiv=0907.3048 |bibcode=2009PhRvD..80f1701K |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.80.061701 |s2cid=36700928}}</ref> This provides non-trivial examples for DeWitt’s proposed mechanism for the quantum resolution of space-time singularities.

=== General relativity ===
D. Korotkin and H. Nicolai explored the [[Ernst equation]] on an arbitrary [[Riemannian surface]]. The Ernst equation was already known to help with the construction of exact [[Stationary process|stationary]] [[Rotational symmetry|axisymmetric]] solutions of [[Einstein's equations]]. As a particular application this work derived a periodic analog of the [[Schwarzschild metric|Schwarzschild solution]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Korotkin |first1=D. |last2=Nicolai |first2=H. |date=October 1994 |title=The ernst equation on a riemann surface |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0550321394800480 |journal=Nuclear Physics B |language=en |volume=429 |issue=1 |pages=229–254 |doi=10.1016/S0550-3213(94)80048-0 |arxiv=gr-qc/9405032 |bibcode=1994NuPhB.429..229K }}</ref> In the 2000s, with T. Damour and M. Henneaux, Nicolai investigated the behavior of the Einstein equations close to a space-like [[gravitational singularity]] such as the [[Big Bang]], following pioneering work of Belinsky, Khalatnikov and Lifshitz ([[BKL singularity|BKL]]). They reformulated general relativity in terms of chaotic [[Dynamical billiards|cosmological billiard]] systems that allow a general analysis of such singularities for spacetimes of any dimensionality and any menu of matter fields.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Damour |first1=T |last2=Henneaux |first2=M |last3=Nicolai |first3=H |date=2003-05-07 |title=Cosmological billiards |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0264-9381/20/9/201 |journal=Classical and Quantum Gravity |volume=20 |issue=9 |pages=R145–R200 |doi=10.1088/0264-9381/20/9/201 |issn=0264-9381|arxiv=hep-th/0212256 }}</ref>
